articles.title: Comprehensive Exhibition Celebrating David Lynch's Unique Photography Opens in Los Angeles
articles.excerpt: Pace Gallery in Los Angeles presents the first posthumous exhibition celebrating the surreal and striking photographic works of David Lynch.
articles.content: Pace Gallery in Los Angeles is hosting the first posthumous exhibition dedicated to the photographs of director and artist David Lynch, who passed away last year. Drawing significant crowds, the presentation encapsulates the idiosyncratic and surreal perspective that defined his remarkable creative career. Featuring striking female portraits, multiple exposures, and meticulously documented subjects, the exhibition highlights the unwavering dedication Lynch brought to his artistic practice. His son Riley Lynch, alongside gallery representatives, continues the extensive effort to preserve and catalogue this voluminous body of work. Lynch's daily commitment to creation underscores his view that art was not merely a profession, but a fundamental necessity of life. Alongside his photographs, the showcase includes unique handmade objects and lamps, pointing to a multidisciplinary output that will be celebrated in a major retrospective at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art in 2028 before touring globally. These works permanently capture Lynch's profound relationship with Los Angeles and his enduring zest for creation.
articles.originalTitle: ‘He made something every single day’: David Lynch’s inscrutable photography celebrated in LA show - The Guardian

articles.title: Critical Finding on Haydarpaşa's Foundations: Eighty Percent of Wooden Piles Lost
articles.excerpt: According to reports by TRT Haber, structural assessments conducted during Haydarpaşa Station's restoration revealed that approximately eighty percent of the historical wooden foundation piles have deteriorated or vanished over time.
articles.content: Critical structural evaluations regarding the foundation of Haydarpaşa Station have yielded alarming results. According to reports from TRT Haber, examinations conducted during restoration works revealed that approximately eighty percent of the historical wooden piles supporting the structure have deteriorated and disappeared. This engineering finding highlights the vulnerability of the station's foundational substrate and underscores the necessity of targeted structural reinforcement. As part of ongoing conservation efforts, project engineers are assessing the implications of this timber loss to formulate appropriate stabilization protocols. The findings necessitate comprehensive interventions to secure the load-bearing capacity of the historic terminal building against future settlement risks.

articles.title: Sophie Calle Focuses on Absence and Memory in Margate Exhibition
articles.excerpt: French conceptual artist Sophie Calle opens her first major UK exhibition in decades at Turner Contemporary, bringing together over three decades of work.
articles.content: French conceptual artist Sophie Calle presents a comprehensive exhibition at Turner Contemporary in Margate, bringing together photographs, videos, and installations created between 1986 and 2024. Living in the same Paris apartment for nearly 50 years, the 72-year-old artist explores themes of absence, loss, and mortality through works centered on her late parents and unfinished projects. Following her residency at the Picasso Museum in Paris, the Margate presentation features key series such as The Blind, which records descriptions of beauty by individuals born without sight, and Voir la Mer, capturing residents of Istanbul witnessing the sea for the first time. Reflecting on a career that began as an effort to engage her father, Calle maintains her characteristic balance of intimacy and detachment. Emphasizing that she harbours no regrets, the artist notes that the absence of dependents provides the necessary space and autonomy to sustain her conceptual practice.

articles.title: Singer Ejae Wears an Archival Roberto Capucci Gown at Vogue World in Milan
articles.excerpt: Performing in the opening chapter of Vogue World: Milan, singer Ejae walked the runway in a blue-and-black tiered gown from the archives of Italian master Roberto Capucci.
articles.content: Performing at Vogue World: Milan, singer Ejae walked the runway in a blue-and-black tiered gown from the archives of Italian fashion master Roberto Capucci. Born in Rome in 1930, Capucci originally trained as a sculptor before opening his clothing atelier before the age of 20. Alongside Valentino Garavani and Emilio Pucci, he became a leading designer of the post-World War II era, ushering in an opulent period of Italian design. Known for his sculptural silhouettes and vibrant color play, Capucci's creations reflect the intricate details of handmade Italian artistry. Featured in the show's opening chapter dedicated to the artisanal revolution, the gown highlighted the handmade richness of the era before electricity and industrialization. Reminiscent of royal aesthetics, the look was paired with a Dolce & Gabbana choker featuring a gold and pearl dangling cross. Conceived as a celebration of Italian craft and innovation under creative director Juan Costa, the presentation brought Renaissance-inspired textiles to life on the runway.

articles.title: Dhruv Kapoor Presents Collection Inspired by Time and Decay at Milan Fashion Week
articles.excerpt: Designer Dhruv Kapoor showcased his spring ready-to-wear collection at Milan Fashion Week, blending artisan details with the marks left by nature and time on objects and the human body.
articles.content: Challenging the fast pace of today's future-obsessed reality, Indian designer Dhruv Kapoor sought respite in stillness for his spring ready-to-wear collection at Milan Fashion Week. Observing the rapid modernization in his home country, such as the accelerated construction of the new tech hub Amaravati in Andhra Pradesh, Kapoor chose to embrace the passage of time and the beauty of decay. His mood board featured construction sites, moss-covered rocks, high-tech cable infrastructures, and sun-faded seashells, which echoed throughout the collection. Broad-shouldered blazers, crisp culottes, boxy tops, and pencil skirts were reconfigured with chandelier-like beadwork, tree trunk textures, and pebbled leather. Traditional garments like the sari and lungi were repurposed into crystal-embellished engineered skirts for women and men, alongside patchwork floral shirtdresses. Kapoor also extended his exploration of time and renewal through a capsule collection with Puma and the Royal Challengers Bengaluru cricket team, utilizing deadstock fabrics to create limited-edition track jackets.
articles.originalTitle: Dhruv Kapoor Spring 2027: Finding Beauty in Decay - WWD

articles.title: Details of the Vogue World Celebration Held at Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II in Milan
articles.excerpt: Held at Milan's iconic Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Vogue World: Milan showcased Italian craftsmanship, artistic heritage, and industrial innovation across five distinct thematic acts.
articles.content: Celebrating Italian craft and innovation, Vogue World: Milan transformed the iconic Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II with a procession of models, celebrities, and performers. The event unfolded across five distinct chapters highlighting Italy's cultural heritage. The opening artisanal revolution act brought Renaissance-inspired textiles, rich brocades, and hand-worked surfaces to life. The industrial revolution act shifted to tailored silhouettes and woolen textiles inspired by Turin's manufacturing legacy. The third act celebrated the cinematic mythology of La Dolce Vita and Federico Fellini, honoring the enduring symbol of the Italian diva. In the intermezzo and the age of intelligence chapter, craft and technology converged through intelligent and sustainable textiles reflecting Milan's role as a design hub. The imagination revolution final chapter presented a speculative future built on Italy's extraordinary heritage. Held under the patronage of the Municipality of Milan and Camera Nazionale della Moda Italiana, with artistic contributions from Teatro alla Scala, the event was directed by creative director Juan Costa Paz and supported by presenting sponsors ALO, eBay, Eli Lilly and Company, and Meta Glasses.

articles.title: John Gerrard on Virtual Worlds and the Evolving Landscape of Digital Art
articles.excerpt: Artist John Gerrard examines his virtual worlds built with game-engine technology and the four-movement digital release of his SPIRITS project across the Los Angeles County Museum of Art platform.
articles.content: Artist John Gerrard creates real-time virtual worlds and simulations centered on energy, power, and ecology using game-engine technology in public spaces. Running since the winter of 2025 on the Los Angeles County Museum of Art landing page, his SPIRITS project comprises 96 software art worlds built around lost plastic shoes found across various shores, transformed into three-dimensional images through Gaussian splatting. Viewers can interact with these worlds by touching their screens to generate variable narratives. Each ocean release coincided with specific solar events over a 24-hour period on lacma.org. Gerrard notes that camera phones can produce compelling dimensional worlds that, through artistic intervention, transform into painterly objects or performance sites. Highlighting art tokens as a secure structural foundation on the blockchain, he explains how these systems grant digital art a substantial and collectable provenance. Emphasizing that artificial intelligence cannot replicate the intensive human labor required for such intricate coding and iteration, the artist argues that contemporary culture must work directly within digital conditions. Anticipating a closer convergence between physical exhibition spaces and global digital networks in the coming decades, Gerrard continues his exploratory work, including his role as a system thinker at the Van Abbemuseum.
articles.originalTitle: Are touchscreens the next art frontier? Digital pioneer John Gerrard thinks so - Art Basel

articles.title: The Gallery House in Pristina Designed by Maden Architects as a Contemporary Residence
articles.excerpt: Designed by Maden Architects in Pristina, Kosovo, the 754-square-meter Gallery House is a contemporary residence establishing continuous visual and spatial connections with its natural surroundings.
articles.content: Located in Pristina, Kosovo, the Gallery House was designed by Maden Architects as a residential property that merges architecture, natural light, spatial movement, and landscape into a calm living experience. Spanning 754 square meters, the building is conceived around the concept of architecture as a continuous journey rather than a compartmentalized arrangement of rooms. Clean geometric volumes establish a distinct architectural identity, while carefully proportioned window openings, interior courtyards, and landscaped zones create an uninterrupted visual and spatial dialogue between the interior and the external environment. The design team focused on generating a refined domestic atmosphere supported by high material quality and thoughtful spatial sequencing. Fixtures and elements from manufacturers such as Artemide, B&T, Flos, and Vondom complement the interior vocabulary. The residence functions as a serene retreat within its urban context, emphasizing a balanced coexistence between built form and nature.

articles.title: Tato Architects Completes Charred Timber-Clad Residence in Japan
articles.excerpt: Completed in Tochigi Prefecture, Japan, the 108-square-metre House in Mibu pairs charred cedar cladding with warm plywood interiors. Designed by Kobe-based Tato Architects, the residence establishes a nuanced spatial balance between enclosure and openness on a compact urban site.
articles.content: Kobe-based studio Tato Architects has completed House in Mibu, a 108-square-metre residence located in Tochigi Prefecture, Japan. Designed for a family on the backyard site of the client's parental home, the dwelling navigates existing access requirements for an adjacent workshop and garage. The exterior features charred cedar cladding paired with a corrugated metal roof to harmonize with the neighboring structures. Studio founder Yo Shimada noted that the core design concept references Dutch architect Aldo van Eyck's spatial philosophy of the in-between zone. To achieve a balance between openness and enclosure, the ground floor is sunk 500 millimetres into the earth and partially crowned with a green roof, while the upper level features a prominent overhang. Entry occurs beneath this upper volume, leading into a cloakroom and bathroom area that steps down into a sunken living, dining, and kitchen space. Full-height western glazing wraps the lower level, fostering a direct connection to the ground and adjacent workshop views. Interiors are finished uniformly in lauan lauan plywood, chosen for its ability to patina gracefully over time. A pair of timber and green-painted steel staircases ascend to the upper floor, where children's bedrooms flank a raised loft area positioned 690 millimetres above the floor plate. This elevated platform functions as a study zone or secondary sleeping space while maintaining visual continuity throughout the interior.
articles.originalTitle: Tato Architects completes charred timber-clad home in Japan - Dezeen

articles.title: Vanguard Underwater Habitat off the Florida Keys Sets the Stage for Marine Research
articles.excerpt: Installed off the Florida Keys by ocean engineering firm DEEP, the four-person Vanguard underwater habitat serves as a pilot structure for more ambitious future marine projects.
articles.content: International ocean engineering and technology firm DEEP has established a new underwater research habitat approximately 60 feet below the surface within the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary. Known as Vanguard, the four-person habitat serves as a pilot structure designed to pave the way for larger, modular underwater projects in the future. Constructed primarily from an existing industrial decompression chamber, the main cylindrical hull features living quarters, a galley, scientific equipment, and a dedicated workspace that doubles as a saturation diving decompression chamber. A bolt-on steel wet porch featuring a moon pool allows divers to easily enter and exit the facility. Following meticulous permitting coordination with the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, subsea surveys including bathymetric, geotechnical, and biological assessments were conducted by Unique Group. To secure the habitat against powerful storm currents and wave energy, the installation relies on a 220-ton base plate anchored by steel piles driven into the underlying limestone. Connected to a surface support buoy via umbilical lines for power, oxygen, and communications, Vanguard is currently undergoing commissioning by DNV. The habitat is expected to welcome its first paying researchers and divers later this year, with remote monitoring maintained around the clock from DEEP's facilities.
articles.originalTitle: Underwater habitat off Florida Keys sets stage for more ambitious projects - American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)

articles.title: United States Congress Addresses Funding Responsibilities for Data Center Power Infrastructure Construction
articles.excerpt: The House passed a bill requiring large data centers to cover power infrastructure costs, while Senate discussions stalled over federal requirements. Experts note that surging electricity demand exerts pressure on supply chains and regional grid capacities.
articles.content: The United States House of Representatives voted to advance a federal standard requiring large data centers to fund the power infrastructure constructed to serve their operational needs. Although the legislative measure passed the House, discussions stalled in the Senate amid differing views on whether federal mandates should impose direct requirements on large-load customers. The proposed framework applies to data center campuses exhibiting peak electricity demand of at least 100 megawatts, stipulating that utility rates should recover the full incremental costs of generation, transmission, and distribution upgrades required for service delivery. Customers would also supply financial assurances before utilities initiate infrastructure modifications. While the House approach preserves traditional state regulatory authority over utility rates, lawmakers intend to protect existing ratepayers from infrastructure expenses tied to artificial intelligence expansion. Conversely, alternative legislative proposals in the Senate seek to mandate direct coverage of grid-connection costs for high-demand consumers. Utilities and state regulators are actively developing specialized large-load tariffs and minimum-demand provisions to mitigate risks associated with potential power supply deficits and underutilized assets. Independent research indicates that minimum-demand stipulations are becoming standard practice across utility portfolios. At the same time, heavy power demand from expanding digital infrastructure continues to strain manufacturing supply chains, limiting the availability of custom transformers, gas turbines, and skilled electrical labor.
articles.originalTitle: Congress Takes Aim at Who Pays for Data Center Power Construction - Engineering News-Record

articles.excerpt: South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix has selected Hanmi Global as construction manager for its 4 billion dollar high-bandwidth memory manufacturing and packaging facility in Indiana, with the cleanroom targeted for completion in October 2028.
articles.content: Global chipmaker SK Hynix, headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, has selected Hanmi Global to oversee construction management for its planned 4 billion dollar artificial intelligence memory manufacturing facility on 133 acres in West Lafayette, Indiana. The project focuses on high-bandwidth memory packaging and testing to address surging technological demand. Construction is already underway, with the cleanroom targeted for completion in October 2028. Having handled preconstruction in 2024, Hanmi Global will direct full project management responsibilities, including design, cost, schedule, quality, safety, and partner coordination. The facility requires complex infrastructure, such as cleanrooms, power, water, and gas systems, synchronized precisely with equipment installation. Serving as SK Hynix's primary artificial intelligence memory production hub in the United States, the site will house a production line and an advanced packaging research and development testbed. SK Hynix plans to supply next-generation memory products, packaged and tested on-site, to domestic customers starting in the second half of 2029. High-bandwidth memory technology vertically connects multiple DRAM chips to expand capacity and accelerate data processing speeds. In addition, SK Hynix signed a memorandum of understanding with Purdue University for collaborative research and talent development in advanced packaging technologies. The venture receives financial support through federal semiconductor incentive programs and funding opportunities established by the Department of Commerce.
articles.originalTitle: Construction Manager Chosen for $4B AI Memory Plant in Indiana - Engineering News-Record
